subject: Is there a way around dist.breaks in distsamp?

messages.author: dcaf23790c09a94d
messages.subject: Is there a way around dist.breaks in distsamp?
parts:
Hi all,

My distance data is already binned, therefore I do not need the dist.breaks function. Is there a way to eliminate or work around it so I can get the yDat function to work?

yDat <-formatDistData(dists, distCol="DistanceID", transectNameCol="Transect_Name", dist.breaks=)

Thanks!

Cheers,
Tim Schreckengost
Master's Candidate
Department of Entomology and Wildlife Ecology
University of Delaware

messages.author: 3fcf0e009c95d23e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Is there a way around dist.breaks in distsamp?
parts:
Hi Tim,

I don't think you need to use formatDistData.  Function unmarkedFrameDS just needs an M x J matrix where M is the number of sites and J is the number of distance bins and values are the number of detections.  So any function that gets your data into the right format will work.

Since your data are already binned, you can use functions melt and cast to reshape it into the MxJ matrix.  Or xtabs.  Or format your data as a matrix before you import it into R.

Cheers,
Chris Merkord
